draft.title: How production affects places
card: Production is making goods from natural resources. Mining, farming, forestry and factories all do this, and each one changes the place where it happens.
Jobs
Production can bring work and income to a town. A mine or factory may employ local people, and shops and services nearby may grow as a result.
Pollution
Production can release waste into air, water and soil. Smoke from a factory or runoff from a farm can harm people, plants and animals.
Cleared land
Mines, farms and plantations often need land cleared of trees and bush. Clearing can destroy habitat and leave soil open to erosion.
draft.remember: Production can bring jobs to a place, but it can also pollute it and strip its land.

a.q: A new gold mine opens near a small town in Western Australia. Which result is a benefit to the town?
opts: Local people get jobs at the mine
Dust from the mine blows over the town
Bushland is cleared for the mine pit
Waste water seeps into nearby soil
a.why: Jobs at the mine give local people work and income, which is a benefit. The other options are harms: dust is pollution, and clearing bushland and waste water damage the land and soil.
a.clue: Which result helps people in the town rather than harming the place?

b.q: A timber company in Tasmania clears native forest and replaces it with rows of one type of tree. It employs 200 local workers. Which statement is best supported?
opts: It gives jobs but also clears land that was habitat
It gives jobs, so it causes no harm to the place
It clears land, so it gives no benefit to the town
It causes pollution, but it does not clear any land
b.why: The company provides jobs, which helps the town, and it clears native forest, which can destroy habitat. Production can bring both effects at once, so saying it has only benefits or only harms is wrong.
b.clue: Look for the option that counts both the jobs and the clearing.

a.best: Local people get jobs at the mine

b.best: It gives jobs but also clears land that was habitat

problems.detail: The clue 'Look for the option that counts both the jobs and the clearing' points straight to the only option that mentions both jobs and clearing, so a student can answer without understanding the idea.

check.summary: The card, remember line and both questions are accurate and match the card. The only problem is that question b's clue gives the answer away by naming the two effects in the right option.
